maria_cs: Hey team — customer (Acme Analytics) seeing intermittent 500s and high tail latency on /v1/generate since ~2024-06-12 10:20 UTC. Sample customer request IDs: req_05f8a2, req_05f8c9, req_06012b. They say the same request sometimes returns 200 quickly and sometimes 500 after ~5s. They attached a curl they used below. Can someone triage?

jordan_eng: Oncall here. Can you paste the exact curl + response headers they got when it 500? Also ask them to include our x-redwood-request-id from the response if present. If they can run with REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 and send the debug bundle that helps. Also please get a minimal SDK repro (py/js/go).

maria_cs: Pasting the curl they sent (sanitized token):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'X-Client-Request-Id: acme-123' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize the following text: ...","max_tokens":64}'
```
Their reported failing response (copy):
```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 10:22:13 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
x-redwood-request-id: 0x5a1f9c8b
Content-Length: 96

{"error":"internal_server_error","message":"oom during decode"}
```
When a request succeeds they sometimes see: HTTP/1.1 200 OK and latency ~520ms. When it 500 latency ~5200ms.

eng_liam: Thanks — to make it quick for eng to reproduce, ask them to run one of these minimal repros locally (use placeholder token). If they can't repro, we'll need the debug bundle and the exact request timestamps + our x-redwood-request-id.

Minimal Python repro (requests):
```python
import requests
url = 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer SK-REPRO-PLACEHOLDER', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Client-Request-Id': 'acme-repro'}
payload = {'model': 'redwood-1.0', 'input': 'Summarize this sentence: The quick brown fox ...', 'max_tokens': 64}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print(resp.status_code, resp.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id'))
print(resp.text)
```

Minimal Node repro (fetch, supports AbortController):
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15000); // 15s hard timeout
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer SK-REPRO-PLACEHOLDER', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Client-Request-Id': 'acme-repro' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Summarize this sentence: The quick brown fox ...', max_tokens: 64 }),
    signal: controller.signal
  });
  console.log(res.status, res.headers.get('x-redwood-request-id'))
  console.log(await res.text());
})();
```

Minimal Go repro (net/http):
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "time"
)
func main() {
  client := &http.Client{ Timeout: 15 * time.Second }
  reqBody := []byte(`{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize this sentence: The quick brown fox ...","max_tokens":64}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(reqBody))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer SK-REPRO-PLACEHOLDER")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Client-Request-Id", "acme-repro")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("err:", err); return }
  fmt.Println("status:", resp.Status)
  fmt.Println("x-redwood-request-id:", resp.Header.Get("x-redwood-request-id"))
}
```

sdk_sam: Quick tips — for Python request sets, always include timeout (no default). For Node use AbortController or a timeout wrapper. For Go set http.Client.Timeout. Also request reuse (keep-alive) can surface transient OOMs if the client pins a long-lived connection to a busy worker. Ask them to retry with a fresh process to rule that out. If they can run the repro repeatedly (100x) we might hit the fail mode.

maria_cs: Forwarded the repros and tips to Acme. They agreed to run the three scripts and to enable REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 in their environment and upload the debug bundle. They've scheduled to run now and will send results + any x-redwood-request-id values. Marking this as high priority — customer revenue impact.

jordan_eng: I'll pick this up if they provide request IDs. Once we have x-redwood-request-id(s) I will pull the logs/traces and correlate to worker-level metrics (GPU memory, OOMs, queue depth). If they reproduce locally we'll try to reproduce with our internal harness too.
